description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is displayed on the x-axis using a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 (1) to 10^3 (1000). The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 60% to 80%, with tick marks at regular intervals of 5%. The Base method is depicted by a black line with circle markers, starting at approximately 61% accuracy at a co-occurrence number of 1 and rising to about 66% at 1000. The MEND method is shown as a brown line with diamond markers, beginning near 66% and increasing to about 74%. The FT method is represented by a blue line with triangle markers, starting near 62% and rising to approximately 68%. The MEMIT method is a purple line with circle markers, beginning at about 66% and increasing to roughly 72%. The IKE method is shown as a red line with triangle markers, starting near 65% and rising to about 70%. The ROME method is depicted by a green line with square markers, starting at approximately 72% and remaining relatively stable near 77% across the entire range of co-occurrence numbers.
